policy: Only read-only scanners and auditors. No resident agents or daemons (no runtime eBPF sensors, no SIEM agents).

Prefer the distro package (signed, security-patched). Otherwise a pinned upstream release at least 14 days old, verified by checksum and signature/provenance when published. Pinned versions and checksums: companion-tools.md.
Sentinel SUGGESTS. Installing anything requires the owner's explicit consent.
Every run writes normalized JSON (schema sentinel-toolbox/v1). Secrets are never written: secret scanners run redacted and only rule/file/line/commit/fingerprint are kept.
Out-of-scope systems: targets, containers and findings matching SENTINEL_SCOPE_EXCLUDE_RE are dropped.

tools.purpose: Kernel audit trail for sensitive files and privileged commands.
tools.why_here: A host without it has no trail of who changed /etc, sshd config, sudoers or systemd units. Filter execve rules by auid so container processes do not flood the log.

tools.purpose: Bans IPs after repeated authentication failures.
tools.why_here: Standard SSH brute-force guard. Note: a firewall rate limit (e.g. ufw limit) produces the same 'Connection refused' symptom with the opposite fix.

tools.purpose: Lists the kernel and services still running old (patched-on-disk) libraries.
tools.why_here: Tells whether an applied security update is actually live, which is exactly the gap after an apt upgrade or a pending reboot.

tools.purpose: Host hardening audit with warnings, suggestions and a 0-100 hardening index.
tools.why_here: Gives a comparable weekly score per host; the drift of the index is the signal.

trust.notes: Shell script, read-only, long-lived project; distributed through the signed distro archive.

tools.purpose: Local TLS/cipher/protocol/certificate audit of our own domains, JSON output.
tools.why_here: Same signal as SSL Labs without depending on a third-party API or its rate limits.

trust.notes: Bash + openssl, no daemon. Scan only our own domains.

tools.purpose: Verifies installed package files against the package checksums (changed binaries/configs).
tools.why_here: Cheap tamper check for system binaries; complements sentinel-baseline without a resident daemon like AIDE.

tools.purpose: Finds secrets committed to git repositories and their history.
tools.why_here: Catches the next committed credential before it reaches a backup or public repo.

trust.channel: distro package (Debian/Ubuntu) (8.16, older rules) or pinned upstream release
trust.notes: Upstream is feature-complete / security-patch-only in 2026; its creator moved to Betterleaks (too new to trust yet). Always run with --redact; the wrapper never stores the secret or match.

tools.purpose: Checks declared dependencies (Gradle/Maven/npm/pip lockfiles) against the OSV database.
tools.why_here: The CVE pipeline sees what is RUNNING; this sees what is DECLARED and will ship in the next deploy.

install.verify: SHA256 from the release checksums file + SLSA provenance when present; version >= 14 days old

tools.weight: medium (DB download + minutes per image, weekly)
tools.purpose: Vulnerabilities in running Docker images, plus misconfiguration and SBOM.
tools.why_here: Covers the images actually running, including bundled runtimes (JVM, Node) the host package manager cannot see.

trust.notes: Supply-chain compromise in March 2026: malicious binary v0.69.4 and Docker images v0.69.5/v0.69.6 (GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23); trivy-action tags were hijacked. Install only a pinned post-incident release, verify cosign signature + checksum, never use floating tags.

install.verify: cosign verify-blob + SHA256; post-incident version only

tools.purpose: CIS Docker Benchmark checks for the daemon, host and running containers.
tools.why_here: Complements sentinel-audit.sh docker with the full CIS list.

trust.channel: git clone at a pinned commit (shell script, auditable)
trust.notes: Do not use the old Docker Hub image; run the script from a reviewed commit.

tools.purpose: Template-based check of our public endpoints for known CVEs and exposures.
tools.why_here: Optional outside-in view. Only our own domains, low rate (Cloudflare in front).

trust.notes: Community templates execute requests; pin the templates version too.

scorecard_note: OpenSSF Scorecard values were read from api.securityscorecards.dev on 2026-11-19; the date in each entry is the date of the scorecard run.
